body:
`tests/test_unified_rejections.py::test_issue_869_and_808_no_stale_chebi_on_local_or_hydrate_records` fails at line 287 because its literal fixture expects `Maltose monohydrate` to keep `cas:6363-53-7` as `mim_id`.

The sourced #1117 conclusion promotes the existing D-maltose monohydrate owner to the exact form-specific `NCIT:C80300`. The reviewed Step 7d native rebuild consequently changes both existing maltose synonym rows to that identifier. This is part of the six traced snapshot cells; it introduces no new membership, status or owner selection. Reverting the identifier merely to satisfy the old fixture would undo the reviewed exact-identity decision under MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3.

Proposed correction: update the bounded maltose expectation to the reviewed exact identity while retaining the stale-CHEBI, mapping-status and all other assertions. Confirm both maltose snapshot rows trace to the same current owner, preserve empty stale-parent CHEBI and all unchanged cases, then run this regression and the full suite.

This needs an explicit additional test-edit authorization: the current user rule permits only the paired companion REVIEW/--review selectors and forbids every other test edit. It is therefore a second Step 7d stop-condition blocker, alongside #1123. Related scientific decision: #1117; umbrella scope: #901.

Observed at Step 7d head `7d35035f6c521c69fad94f73381c6a6eb7251fff`. Full native suite: 5,069 passed, 3 failed, 1 skipped, 33 warnings; exit 1. Receipt: `output/approved-plan-20261101T031134Z/logs/step7d-derived-full-suite-v1.json`; log SHA-256 `ff86736a2115bd2f8fb2031f1ee6e1b99955454a26357df396429a5f5e07df9f`.

The complete live open issue/PR inventory was searched for this defect before filing. No Step 7d push, PR or merge has occurred. The run is stopped under the user's explicit test-change restriction; no fix is applied by filing this issue. No production identity, snapshot cell, approval, assertion or workflow should be weakened to pass a test.
title: Unified snapshot regression still pins maltose monohydrate to its superseded CAS identity
